title: Past HMI spot area reduces but does not remove the Cycle 25 radio offset in matched rising-phase models
abstract: We test whether daily area mixtures or past dark area explain the Cycle 25 emission offset at fixed HMI spot area. In matched rising-phase months in 2011-2013 and 2022-2024, averaging nonlinear daily-area basis functions retains a 14.11 sfu F10.7 offset (conditional 95% interval 8.28 to 20.21). On dates with complete 81-day histories, adding past area reduces the offset from 14.06 to 8.68 sfu (4.33 to 13.33). The paired reduction is 5.38 sfu (0.62 to 10.19). Phase and daily joint-support checks retain a reduction and a positive residual. Mg II also falls but keeps a positive residual. Daily mixtures do not explain the offset within the tested spline family. Past area gives a partial model explanation. This is not a causal physical share. Two cycles, limited support, flexible response functions and unmeasured scale drift prevent physical emission changes from being separated from measurement changes. Code, aggregate estimates, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions are supplied.

display.caption: Cycle 25 offsets after daily-area and past-area controls. Conditional 95% residual-block intervals. Samples and fitted reference levels differ across models.
